function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | • A single pane of glass that aggregates metrics from GCP, AWS, Azure, on‑prem, and edge environments.
• Real‑time dashboards that surface CPU, memory, I/O, network, and application‑level KPIs. | Unilever can see the health of its global supply‑chain, retail, and consumer‑engagement workloads without switching between vendor consoles. | | **AI‑Driven Performance & Cost Optimization** | • Machine‑learning models that learn normal workload patterns and automatically recommend or enact scaling, right‑sizing, and cost‑saving actions.
• Predictive alerts for capacity shortages, SLA violations, or budget overruns. | AI reduces manual tuning, speeds up response times, and keeps spend under control—critical for a multinational FMCG company with tight margins. | | **Policy‑Based Automation** | • Declarative policies that define “what” should happen (e.g., keep latency < 200 ms, stay within $X/month).
• Turbonomics enforces those policies across all clouds via API calls, auto‑scaling, or workload migration. | Unilever can enforce consistent performance standards across regions while still taking advantage of each cloud’s strengths. | | **Cross‑Cloud Workload Migration** | • AI recommends when and where to move workloads (e.g., shift a batch‑processing job from Azure to GCP during off‑peak hours).
• Handles live migration, data replication, and re‑registration of services. | Enables Unilever to avoid vendor lock‑in, optimize for regional compliance, and balance load globally. | | **Integrated Observability Stack** | • Combines telemetry from Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, and vendor APIs into a unified data lake.
• Supports custom metrics and logs from Unilever’s proprietary applications. | Gives a holistic view of performance, security, and compliance—all in one place. | | **Self‑Healing & Auto‑Remediation** | • AI detects anomalies, diagnoses root causes, and automatically triggers remediation workflows (e.g., restart a pod, scale a VM). | Minimizes downtime for critical e‑commerce and supply‑chain services. | #### Practical Example for Unilever 1. **Data‑Analytics Pipeline** – Unilever runs a real‑time analytics pipeline that ingests sales data from stores worldwide. 2. **Observability** – Turbonomics pulls metrics from all three clouds where the pipeline runs. 3. **AI Recommendation** – The platform predicts a spike in traffic during a holiday sale and suggests adding more compute resources in the region with the lowest cost. 4. **Automation** – Turbonomics automatically provisions new VMs in GCP, scales Kubernetes nodes, and updates DNS records. 5. **Cost Control** – After the sale, it recommends shutting down excess resources and moving idle workloads to cheaper spot instances. --- ### Difference Between Turbonomics and Native Cloud Observability Tools | Feature | Turbonomics | GCP Operations (formerly Stackdriver) | AWS CloudWatch | Azure Monitor | |---------|-------------|---------------------------------------|----------------|---------------| | **Scope** | Multi‑cloud + on‑prem | Single‑cloud (GCP) | Single‑cloud (AWS) | Single‑cloud (Azure) | | **Unified Dashboard** | One UI for all clouds | Separate consoles per cloud | Separate consoles per cloud | Separate consoles per cloud | | **AI/ML Capabilities** | Predictive analytics, auto‑optimization, anomaly detection | Basic anomaly detection (metrics alerts) | Basic anomaly detection (alarms) | Basic anomaly detection (alerts) | | **Policy‑Based Automation** | Declarative policies that trigger actions across clouds | Limited automation (Cloud Functions, Cloud Run) | Limited automation (Lambda, Step Functions) | Limited automation (Logic Apps, Functions) | | **Cost Optimization** | AI‑driven right‑size recommendations, spot‑instance bidding, cross‑cloud cost balancing | Cost Explorer, budgets | Cost Explorer, budgets | Cost Management, budgets | | **Workload Migration** | AI‑guided migration, live migration support | No built‑in migration tooling | No built‑in migration tooling | No built‑in migration tooling | | **Integration with Vendor APIs** | Native connectors + OpenTelemetry | Native connectors only | Native connectors only | Native connectors only | | **Observability Depth** | Combines metrics, logs, traces, custom business KPIs | Metrics, logs, traces | Metrics, logs, traces | Metrics, logs, traces | | **Vendor Lock‑In Mitigation** | Designed to avoid lock‑in | Vendor‑specific | Vendor‑specific | Vendor‑specific | #### Key Takeaways 1. **Multi‑Cloud vs. Single‑Cloud** – Turbonomics is built for an environment where workloads span multiple clouds; native tools are confined to their own ecosystem. 2. **AI‑First Optimization** – Turbonomics uses machine learning to proactively manage performance and cost, whereas native tools rely on manual thresholds and alerts. 3. **Unified Policy Engine** – Turbonomics lets you write a single policy that applies everywhere; native tools require separate rules per cloud. 4. **Cross‑Cloud Migration** – Turbonomics can move workloads between clouds automatically; native tools provide no such capability. 5. **Cost Visibility** – Turbonomics aggregates spend across all clouds into one cost dashboard; native tools give you separate cost reports per provider. --- ### Bottom Line for Unilever - **If Unilever wants a single, AI‑powered observability and optimization layer that spans all its cloud deployments**, Turbonomics is the natural fit. - **If Unilever is comfortable managing each cloud separately and doesn’t need cross‑cloud automation**, native tools may suffice, but they will require more manual effort and lack the predictive, policy‑driven automation that Turbonomics offers. By adopting Turbonomics, Unilever can achieve consistent performance, tighter cost control, and greater agility across its global cloud footprint—all while leveraging AI to reduce operational overhead.
